Porters and Stouts. What other kinds of beer could you add coffee too and make it taste better?

As far as this style goes, I'm mostly familiar with the Lagunitas' Cappuccino Stout. This evening I decided to try a 22oz Ballast Point's (San Diego, CA) "Victory At Sea", porter with coffee and vanilla.

Pouring out of the fridge into a chilled pint glass, this porter creates a massive foamy head. It's hands down the smoothest, richest and tastiest dark beer I've ever had. The flavor is abundant but not overwhelming from the first chilly sip, and continues to deepen and expand as it warms up over the hour it should take you to properly enjoy this 10% brew.

As the autumn procedes with it's clear and cold nights, I find porters a nice addition to the repetoire. Can anyone else recommend a nice porter and coffee?
I like my beer the way I like my coffee. Pure, and not adulterated with the other one.

I'm a big fan of the Founders' Porter (self titled) ... It's more on the malty-dark chocolate side...but would definitely go well with a little extra coffee 'kick'. If you haven't..I'd suggest trying it. I'm a bit curious now; how it would taste with an hint or even a more upfront coffee flavor to it.

I had a coffee pale ale that was interesting at a beerfest. I know it was an NC brewery, just can't remember which one.

I plan to do a coffee brown for a christmas eve party. My relatives are more of the bud drinkers so I don't want to weigh them down with a heavy porter or stout. I want to have a little more body than the normal brown but still be within specs.

As for your actual question, if you are local to NC I have a number of suggestions. If not, I really like Terrapin's Wake n Bake, which is a coffee imperial oatmeal stout. It's good for those days when you want a couple beers and to also feel like you have had a full meal.
